name: Toro
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress
sweep_summary: Toro (toro1249, Turkwam/Atoro [tdv], Alumic Plateau, Nigeria) is not in the catalog, and this search of works with stress in the title turned up no statement about its word stress. The single title-hit, Tallman 2021 (Journal of Linguistics 57(1):208-214, DOI 10.1017/S0022226720000456), is a paywalled book review of Féry's 'Intonation and prosodic structure' that Glottolog tags to Toro only by an automated page-number match; the Cambridge preview mentions no Toro/Turkwam/Atoro. Verified via Glottolog JSON that the languoid's whole reference list is Blench 2006 (wordlist, 23 pp.), Decker et al. 2021 (SIL sociolinguistic survey), and three mis-tags (Bobes 1992, Shnukal 1999, Tallman 2021). The two real sources were already held by the project at (, , ) and were re-read: Blench's section 3.3 'Tones' is an empty heading and p.1 says 'In general, tones are not marked'; Decker et al. Appendix F says there was 'no in-depth analysis of tones or other phonological or phonetic features'; neither mentions stress or accent. Wikipedia's Toro page has no phonology section; No item to prioritize for acquisition; there is no known first-hand description of Toro stress. Notes appended to

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid page and JSON for toro1249 (glottolog.org)
sources.note: Bibliography only: Blench 2006 (wordlist) is the sole genuine descriptive ref; no grammar, sketch or phonology listed. Bobes 1992, Tallman 2021, Shnukal 1999 in the target record are mis-tags unrelated to Toro.

sources.citation: Decker, Ken, David Onoja, Innocent Jonah, John Muniru & Samuel Eju. 2021. A Sociolinguistic Profile of the Arum (Alumu-Tesu) [aab] and Atoro [tdv] Languages of Nasarawa State, Nigeria. Journal of Language Survey Reports 2021-048. SIL International. 60 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 8.3-8.5 (pp. 18-21) give Arum/Atoro consonant and vowel inventories and segmental correspondences only; Appendix F p.36: 'The transcriptions are preliminary since there was no in-depth analysis of tones or other phonological or phonetic features.' Wordlists carry tone diacritics but no prosodic analysis; no mention of stress.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2012 printout (June 11, 2012) of the same work, 'The Toro language of Central Nigeria and its affinities', KWEF Cambridge, 21 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Identical structure to the 2010 printout; 3.3 Tones still empty; no mention of stress.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2010. The Toro language of Central Nigeria and its affinities. Draft circulated for comment, printout August 30, 2010. Cambridge: Kay Williamson Educational Foundation. 21 pp. (= Glottolog's 'Blench 2006' Mallam Dendo MS; cited by Decker et al. as Blench 2010b)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 3 Phonology (pp. 2-3) is 'based on rapid observations.. tentative': 3.1 seven-vowel chart, 3.2 consonant chart, 3.3 'Tones' is an empty heading with no text; p.1: 'In general, tones are not marked, although the data was taped'. No occurrence of stress/accent/prominence anywhere in the 21 pp.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2004. Tarok and related languages of east-central Nigeria (MS; formerly at rogerblench.info/Language/Niger-Congo/BC/Plateau/Tarokoid/)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Comparative paper that first grouped Alumu, Tesu and Toro; could contain brief phonological remarks on Toro, though classification-focused. rogerblench.info is now squatted; Internet Archive copy not downloaded.
No phonology; references only Ethnologue, Blench 2004 (Tarokoid subclassification) and Blench 2010 Toro wordlist.
